title: Fibrewise regular germs cut a flat slice of a scheme morphism
statement: Let $g:T\to B$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $t\in T$, put $b=g(t)$, and suppose $g$ is flat at $t$ [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Let $r\geq0$ and let $h_1,\ldots,h_r\in\mathcal O_{T,t}$ have images forming a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] in the local ring $\mathcal O_{T_b,t}$ of the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Then there are an affine open neighbourhood $W\subseteq T$ of $t$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and sections $a_1,\ldots,a_r\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ with germs $h_i$, such that $t\in D=V(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\subseteq W$ and $D\to B$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Here $D$ is the closed subscheme defined by the ideal generated by the $a_i$ [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Tag 06LI (lemma-slice-given-elements), forgetting the additional regular-immersion and arbitrary-base-change regular-immersion conclusions; r=0 is the empty-equation case.

proof.text: We prove the assertion by induction on the length $r$, for all morphisms and all specified germs satisfying its hypotheses. First choose an affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ through $t$ mapping into an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq B$, with $R$ finitely presented over $A$, using local finite presentation. The affine-stalk localization statement writes each $h_i=u_i/v_i$ in $R_{\mathfrak q}$, with $v_i\notin\mathfrak q$, where $\mathfrak q$ represents $t$. Replace $U$ by the principal open for $v=\prod_i v_i$ (take $v=1$ if $r=0$). It is affine, and all the $h_i$ are represented by sections $b_i=u_i/v_i$ there. This restriction remains locally of finite presentation: a presentation $R=A[X_1,\ldots,X_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m)$ gives $R_v=A[X_1,\ldots,X_n,z]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m,z\widetilde v-1)$, where $\widetilde v$ represents $v$. Its stalks at $t$, including the fibre stalk, are unchanged by this open restriction. Rename this open $U$.

source.place: Tag 06LI, lemma-slice-given-elements, first proof: affine restriction and extension of the finitely many germs, as also in the second proof

proof.text: For $r=0$, apply the compatible-affine-charts flat-locus lemma with $S=Y=B$, $X=U$, $p=f=g|_U$ and $q=\mathrm{id}_B$. The identity is locally of finite type, since on an affine chart its algebra is generated by the empty set. The lemma gives an open neighbourhood $E$ of $t$ in $U$ consisting of points where $g$ is flat: the chart flat locus contains $t$ by the assumed flatness there. Choose a principal open $W\subseteq U$ containing $t$ and contained in $E$, using the basic-open basis. On $W$ all stalk maps are flat, so $W\to B$ is flat. The explicit localization presentation of Step 1 shows that it is locally of finite presentation. With no equations $D=V(0)=W$, proving the base case.

source.place: Tag 06LI, lemma-slice-given-elements, first proof: empty-equation case, using openness of flatness (theorem-openness-flatness)

proof.text: Suppose $r=k+1>0$ and the assertion has been proved for length $k$. Put $C=\mathcal O_{T_b,t}$ and write $\bar h_i$ for the images of the germs in $C$. The regular-sequence definition says that the final quotient $C/(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_r)$ is nonzero. Every prefix quotient surjects onto this quotient, hence is nonzero, and its required multiplication maps are among those of the original sequence. Thus the length-$k$ prefix is regular. Each $h_i$ belongs to the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{T,t}$: if it were a unit its image in $C$ would be a unit, forcing the final quotient to vanish. Apply the induction hypothesis to $g|_U$ and this prefix. It gives an affine $W_0=\operatorname{Spec}R_0\subseteq U$ through $t$, sections $a_1,\ldots,a_k$ with the prescribed germs, and $D_0=\operatorname{Spec}(R_0/I)$ containing $t$, flat and locally of finite presentation over $B$, where $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$. For $k=0$ this is the base case, with $I=0$. Let $b_r$ be the restriction to $W_0$ of the last section chosen in Step 1.

source.place: Tag 06LI, lemma-slice-given-elements, first proof: the induction on r; properness of the ideal and the explicit prefix induction hypothesis

proof.text: The fibre local ring of $D_0\to B$ at $t$ is canonically $C/(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_k)$, preserving the last equation. Here is the affine calculation, so no regular-immersion claim is needed. Choose an affine base chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq B$ containing the image of $W_0$ as in Step 1, put $K=\kappa(b)$ and $E=R_0\otimes_A K$, and let $P$ be the fibre prime at $t$. The affine fibre-product and stalk statements give $C=E_P$. The maps $\bar u\otimes\lambda\mapsto[u\otimes\lambda]$ and $[u\otimes\lambda]\mapsto\bar u\otimes\lambda$ are inverse homomorphisms $(R_0/I)\otimes_A K\simeq E/IE$: the defining bilinear relations and the relations $I=0$ hold in both rings. Localizing gives $(E/IE)_{P/IE}\simeq E_P/IE_P$ by $\bar u/\bar v\leftrightarrow[u/v]$, since the allowed denominators are exactly those outside $P$. The generators $a_i$ map to $\bar h_i$, and $b_r$ maps to the class of $\bar h_r$. This proves the asserted identification and its compatibility with the specified germ.

source.place: Tag 06LI, lemma-slice-given-elements, first proof: the induction on r: fibre of a successive closed slice and its quotient local ring, written out

proof.text: Let $\eta$ be the germ of the image of $b_r$ in $\mathcal O_{D_0,t}$. It lies in the maximal ideal, since $h_r$ does and the stalk map of the closed immersion is local. By Step 4 and regularity of the original sequence, its image in the fibre local ring of $D_0$ is a nonzerodivisor. The single-equation flat-hypersurface lemma now applies to $D_0\to B$: local finite presentation and flatness at $t$ were supplied by induction, and its germ hypothesis has just been checked. It gives an affine open $V\subseteq D_0$ through $t$, a section $c$ on $V$ with germ $\eta$, and a closed subscheme $H=V(c)\subseteq V$ containing $t$, flat and locally of finite presentation over $B$.

source.place: Tag 06LI, lemma-slice-given-elements, first proof: apply the r=1 result to the next slice; Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element

proof.text: The sections $c$ and the image of $b_r$ on $V$ have equal germs at $t$. By the stalk equality criterion they agree on an open neighbourhood $N\subseteq V$ of $t$. In the affine scheme $D_0=\operatorname{Spec}(R_0/I)$ choose a basic open $D(\bar s)$ with $t\in D(\bar s)\subseteq N$. Lift $\bar s$ to $s\in R_0$ and set $W=D(s)\subseteq W_0$. The prime of $t$ contains $I$, so $\bar s$ avoiding that quotient prime implies that $s$ avoids the prime of $t$ in $R_0$. Thus $W$ is an affine neighbourhood of $t$ in the original $T$, and $D_0\cap W=\operatorname{Spec}(R_0/I)_{\bar s}=D(\bar s)$. On $W$ take the restrictions of $a_1,\ldots,a_k$ and put $a_r=b_r|_W$. The closed subscheme they define has coordinate ring $(R_0)_s/(a_1,\ldots,a_k,b_r)$. It equals $H\cap D(\bar s)$ scheme-theoretically: both coordinate rings are $((R_0/I)_{\bar s})/(\bar b_r)$, since $c=\bar b_r$ there. The identification sends the class of $u/s^n$ to the class of $\bar u/\bar s^n$, with inverse induced by the same representatives. In particular it is an open subscheme of $H$.

source.place: Tag 06LI, lemma-slice-given-elements, first proof: the induction on r: realize the successive slice by equations on one affine open of the original scheme

proof.text: The open subscheme $D=H\cap D(\bar s)$ is flat over $B$, because its stalks and stalk maps at each point are those of $H$. It is locally of finite presentation over $B$ as well: at any of its points take a finite-presentation affine chart of $H\to B$, shrink inside this open by a principal open, and use the explicit extra-variable localization presentation in Step 1. The affine-open and basic-open basis statements supply those shrinks. Every final section still has germ $h_i$ by restriction, and $t\in D$ because it lies in $H$ and $D(\bar s)$. This proves the induction step, hence the assertion for every $r\geq0$.
